entry_points.text: Fixed opaque transfer reserves room, copies bytes and reports aligned size. Decode obtains contiguous windows, copies out and skips padding, mapping short input to malformed signals with wrappers warning once or reporting input-output failure.

Size estimation adds per-entry allowances with minimum counts. Hotplug binds callbacks with priority while device conversion recovers enclosing nodes. Speculation helpers mask out-of-bounds indexes and clamp with width checks.

Tree insertion generates identifiers before raw linking. When provider support is unavailable, registration and cell or layout creation report not-supported, unregister does nothing and container lookup returns null.

exports.text: One operations vector centralizes per-version behavior for mount and lifecycle, namespace and links, attributes and sizes, paged transfer with setup and completion, locking, open contexts, delegations and swap.

Namespace helpers derive shared headers from carriers, init or free with per-type numbers and ops, manage passive and active counts tolerating null, select current instances, and locate global per-type trees.

Provider callbacks abstract register access and cell fixup, layout drivers bind registration with module ownership, pools pop from any slot but push to the current CPU with interrupts disabled, and annotations record unwind and reachability metadata.

hazards.text: Trailing arrays sized by separate counts, page vectors with base and length, plus and end flags, scratch lifetimes, single-bit sharing, short opaque input and publish-head skew risk overrun, shape errors or leaks.

Authentication allows twelve flavors with lowest-bit truncation. Inline vectors hold eight pages. Four-byte units round upward. Access lists allow 1024 entries. Memory lifecycle uses single-bit flags. Client identity is 64-bit. Pathnames allow 512 components. Binding retries three times. Security styles use zero and one.

Clone aggregate ORs all flags. Nonvolatile kinds run zero through four with minus-one and minus-two sentinels. Aggregation uses invalid root identity with greedy only. Pools cap count at one shifted by twenty-four and size at one shifted by sixteen. Unwind types run zero through seven.

invariants.text: Version four carriers open with session sequencing and select attributes through mask pointers that may use inline stores, while legacy three has none. Bulk data uses caller pages with base and length, and change info pairs with directory attributes.

Release helpers run under read-side protection and drop the network only when file release requests it. Close, init, disable, cache, performance, notifier and device helpers in this configuration accept arguments and succeed without effect.

Namespace kinds pair with clone flags in one reused list. Initial checks use reserved ranges and warn on zero. Tree membership links with raw variants, unlinks, and reports attached state. Headers use once-only inclusion guards with build-dependent warnings.

Several referenced helpers for bounds, atomic updates, interrupt masking, processor identity and reference counting are owned elsewhere. Only their reliance is recorded here without describing internals.

locks.text: Commit arrays combine reference counts with deferred reclamation. Local identity keeps a private cache-aligned spin guard, delegates list protection externally, and holds network context under read-copy-update for safe release.

Pool access disables local interrupts and relies on atomic positions without sleeping. Namespace final release can atomically acquire a caller spinlock, and shared headers carry read-copy-update nodes for deferred freeing.

state_machines.text: Header dispositions steer retry and completion, separating terminal error and end from redo, status checks, layout versus metadata resubmission, unstable-write handling and direct mode.

Namespaces pin initial instances and allow conditional acquisition otherwise with combined drop and lock handling. Pool slots separate reservation from visibility with acquire reserve, store, release publish and reload on skewed views.

structs.text: Close, lock and delegation carriers group sequencing with handles, state identities, ranges and owners. Lock adds blocking, reclaim and new-owner marks. Test reports conflicting ranges on denial, and return carries masks, layout exchange and time updates.

Paged transfer shares sequencing, handle, contexts, offset, length and pages with direction tails for expected length or masks and stability. Results add counts, end flags and verifiers. Commit, remove and rename add ranges or names with change info.

Authentication pairs length with fixed flavor storage. Directory entries carry numbers, cookies, names, handles and types. Legacy and version three carriers stay handle-centric with names, guards, masks, verifiers and page vectors for data and listings.

Version four access, create, getattr, lookup and directory operations pair sequencing with masks and names. Create diverges for symlinks and devices. Responses return handles, attributes, change info and optional delegation or verifier state.

Client setup, capability discovery, filesystem locations and security negotiation describe servers, masks and flavors with counts. Session setup adds protection and channel attributes with binding. Parallel commit tracks per-bucket queues with verifiers.

Version 4.2 allocation, copy, offload status, notification, seek and extended attributes share sequencing envelopes with handles, ranges, progress and paging. Small page collections pair an external pointer with embedded storage for common sizes.

Transfer headers aggregate file context, credentials, pages, segments, callbacks and retry state. Commit separates policy, inode context and per-operation data. Local server operations support open and alignment queries. Nodes embed devices with access and cache descriptors.

Shared namespace headers hold type, numbers, stashed paths and embedded tree state with read-copy-update nodes. Roots combine balanced trees with lists, and per-namespace state adds identifiers, counts and owner linkage.

Nonvolatile entries record keepouts and cells with geometry and fixup hooks. Configuration binds devices, cells, layouts and callbacks. Layouts embed devices with add-cells operations. Aggregation pairs object sizes with delta and root handlers plus accounting.

Pool slots track head, tail and publish positions over flexible arrays. Pool headers record sizing, counts, flags and release callbacks. Unwind records capture addresses, stack state, type tags and signal marks.
